full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that the appellants (plaintiffs) instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 1999 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Satkhira for specific performance of contract in respect of 3.49 acres of land of Plot No. 9879 of, S.A. Khatian Nos. 2257 and 2292 out of 8.661 acres of land. Plaintiffs case in short is that the respondent No. 1 (defendant) entered to a contract for sale of the suit land with the plaintiff on 14th September, 1989 at a consideration of Tk. 1,05,000/- and on receipt of advance amount of Tk. 60,000/- delivered possession of the same on condition that he would execute and register a sale deed within 13th Jaistha, 1397 B.S. upon receipt of the balance amount of Tk. 45,000/-. The plaintiffs offered the balance consideration amount and requested the defendant to execute the sale deed but the latter refused to perform his part of obligation. 

 9. Moreso, in the plaint the plaintiffs claimed that they entered into the contract in respect of 3.49 acres of land out of 8.66 acres of land of S.A. Plot No. 9879 of S.A. Khatian Nos. 2257 and 2292 without giving the specific boundary of the suit land and thus it is apparent that the suit land is vague and indefinite. Under such circumstances even if the plaintiffs get a decree for specific performance, they will not be able to execute the decree since the suit land is vague and not identifiable. The contract sought to be enforced must be certain, unambiguous, mutual and, upon a valuable consideration; it must be fair in all its parts; free from any misrepresentation, imposition or surmise, not an unconscionable; and its performance not oppressive upon the defendant and finally it must be capable of execution through a decree of the Court. A contract cannot be specifically enforced by a Court if it is not mutual. It is also utmost important that the plaintiff should come into Court in clean hands. Mr. Mahbubey Alam frankly concedes that since the plaintiffs are cultivating shrimp over a vast water logged area including the suit land it is difficult for the plaintiffs to give specific boundary of the suit land. This explanation suggests the vagueness of the suit land. A person who sets up a false ease should not, therefore, expect a Court of equity to grant him such relief.
